newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Merrill Lynch meets Belgrade officials - report.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch meets Belgrade officials - report.

text.p: A senior Merrill Lynch official met representatives of the Serbian government and Yugoslav banks in Belgrade on Thursday to discuss the country's return to the world markets, Yugoslav news agency Tanjug said.

Dan Stratan, Merrill Lynch vice-president for the Balkans and Eastern Europe met Serbian deputy prime minister Slobodan Babic and Dusan Vlatkovic, minister of finance, said Tanjug quoting a Serbian information ministry statement.
"Our primary goal is a concrete support to Yugoslavia's return to the world's financial markets," Stratan said.
In that sense, Merrill Lynch is interested to return to Yugoslavia and the local market, he said. Stratan also met Yugoslav central bank vice-governor Zarko Trbojevic.
Both sides will soon meet again to discuss precise forms of cooperation, the agency said without giving any details.
The United Nations in October 1996 lifted a tough trade and oil embargo on Yugoslavia, now comprising Serbia and Montenegro, imposed in May 1992 for its role in Bosnian war.

But Yugoslavia's access to the international financial organisations and institutions was still blocked by an "outer wall" of sanctions that Washington intends to keep in place until Serbia improves its human rights record.
